_spec.README: THE WIRE TABLE. This file is the single source of truth for which lifecycle hooks are registered, under which event, on both agents. hooks.sh READS _spec.wire and registers each row through bootstrap_settings_merge (the one writer) — it never copies this file into place, so the _spec block never reaches a user's machine. The top-level hooks object below is the rendered Copilot envelope, kept so a human can see exactly what lands; verify_hooks asserts it still agrees with _spec.wire, because two renderings of one table drift silently.

paths.why_user_tier: MEASURED: Copilot repo-level hooks (.github/hooks/*.json) are TRUST-GATED — an identical hook set fired from ~/.copilot/hooks and wrote nothing from the repo until the folder was trusted. The user tier has no such gate, so a bootstrap must use it and the gesture never arises.
paths.why_pascalcase: MEASURED: PascalCase event names are Copilot's documented VS Code compatible format. Six of them fired; six near-miss controls (SessionStarted, PreToolUsage, AgentStop, USERPROMPTSUBMIT, sessionstart, NotAnEventXYZ) stayed silent, so resolution is an exact-string alias table, not case folding. Registered this way, Copilot's stdin payload is field-for-field Claude Code's snake_case — including tool_name: Bash — so one script serves both agents with no shim. QUALIFIED by the first divergence below: that holds for the FIELD NAMES, not for every tool's payload SHAPE — the edit tool's tool_input is a string, not an object.

divergences: THE BIG ONE, MEASURED LIVE on 1.0.83 and NOT what the docs imply: Copilot's file-editing tool arrives as tool_name "Edit" with tool_input a STRING holding an apply-patch envelope (*** Begin Patch / *** Delete File: <path> / *** Add File: <path>), so tool_input.file_path DOES NOT EXIST and the write is a whole-file delete-then-add. A Claude-Code-shaped write guard matches nothing there and backs up nothing: the first live run of guard-write.sh under Copilot saved NOTHING before this was found. guard-write.sh now reads the paths out of the patch header lines, and its fixtures carry that payload verbatim. Note the corollary: "Edit" is the one tool name we deliberately ignore on Claude Code, where an Edit is a targeted replacement.
PostToolUse gives tool_result{result_type,text_result_for_llm} where Claude Code gives tool_response. None of the three hooks here uses PostToolUse; a future one must branch on that field.
Copilot preToolUse FAILS CLOSED: exit 2, a crash, or any non-zero exit denies the tool call even if stdout says allow. Every exit path in every hook here is an explicit 0.
Copilot agentStop does not list systemMessage as an output field, so stop.sh sends arms A and B to stderr there and keeps JSON for the decision only.
Copilot's sessionStart additionalContext was observed PARSED (hook.end) but was not observed reaching the model under copilot -p. Emitting it is free; do not depend on it.
_spec.matcher_policy: Claude Code matches PreToolUse on tool_name, so the write guard carries Write|MultiEdit there. Copilot's write tool turned out to be called "Edit" (measured), which a Write|MultiEdit matcher would have missed entirely, so the Copilot row carries NO matcher — an omitted matcher is every tool — and guard-write.sh filters in-script. An empty matcher string is NOT a wildcard in Copilot (it is a regex), which is why the field is omitted rather than set to "".

unwired.guard-bash.sh: INSTALLED BUT DELIBERATELY NOT REGISTERED. It false-allowed rm -rf on a quoted $HOME and a quoted force-push to trunk; the rewrite fixes that and proves it with a quoted matrix, but a guard believed present and inert is worse than one known absent. verify_hooks ASSERTS its absence from both settings files. See the header of guard-bash.sh and its --wire-me-instructions.

wire.does: Injects the frozen scope, the previous session's ledger and a LIVE git read as additionalContext. Never blocks.
Ledger + context-fill advisory + a BOUNDED auto-continue that may return decision:block. Bounded by stop_hook_active and a per-session counter (BOOTSTRAP_STOP_MAX, default 3).
Backs a file up before a whole-file write and asks for integration rather than replacement. Advisory only; never blocks.
